title: What was Operation Plowshare?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explain Operation Plowshare, the 1957–1977 U.S. Atomic Energy Commission program to use peaceful nuclear detonations for civil engineering projects such as canals, harbors, and mining. They trace its origins to the 1956 Suez Crisis and Herbert York's idea, named after Isaiah's "beat swords into plowshares." They cover early tests (Gnome, Sedan, Buggy), proposed projects (Carryall, Chariot in Alaska, sea-level canals, the Kapingamarangi reef), fallout and environmental opposition, and the gas stimulation (fracking) experiments that proved costly and tritium-contaminated. The episode ends with listener mail about John Hodgman's nostalgia-episode rebuttal and a listener email on gender and job choice.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Operation Plowshare
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the show intro and introduce Operation Plowshare, the idea of using surplus atomic bombs for earth-moving civil engineering, and mention a Slate excerpt on the topic.

segments.title: Suez Crisis background
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1956 Suez Crisis: Nasser nationalizing the Suez Canal, Anglo-French anger, Israel's invasion at their urging, and Soviet and American responses that ended the crisis.

segments.title: Origins of Plowshare and Rainier shot
segments.summary: Herbert York proposes using nuclear weapons for earth moving, the name comes from Isaiah, and the Rainier shot under Operation Plumb Bob proves fully contained underground testing is possible.

segments.title: Moratoriums and restart of testing
segments.summary: Khrushchev and Eisenhower's testing moratorium, its collapse amid Berlin and U-2 tensions, and the 1961 restart that let Plowshare resume testing.

segments.title: Proposed projects: reef channel, canals, and Nevada
segments.summary: Edward Teller's group proposed blowing a channel through the Kapingamarangi reef and sea-level canals, including ideas for widening the Panama Canal, with a brief digression about Nevada pronunciation.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts take a break before resuming the Plowshare story.

segments.title: Operation Gnome and Operation Sedan
segments.summary: Operation Gnome in a New Mexico salt mine produced heat and a cavity, followed by Operation Sedan in Nevada, a 104-kiloton blast creating the largest man-made crater in America and releasing large fallout. A Soviet crater lake in Kazakhstan is mentioned.

segments.title: Operation Buggy and gas stimulation
segments.summary: Operation Buggy chained five 1-kiloton charges to create a channel. Gas stimulation experiments used nuclear blasts to free natural gas, but tritium contamination and high costs ended the approach.

segments.title: Operation Carryall and Operation Chariot
segments.summary: Operation Carryall proposed blowing a valley through a southern California mountain range for highways and rail lines. Operation Chariot proposed an artificial harbor in Alaska, opposed by local Inuit groups and environmentalists, and was dropped after public pushback.

segments.title: End of Plowshare
segments.summary: Public fallout fears and the environmental movement, along with cheaper alternatives, led to the end of Operation Plowshare. The program ran twelve years with 27 experiments and 35 bombs.

segments.title: Listener mail: John Hodgman and gender pay gap
segments.summary: Hosts read a note from John Hodgman responding to their nostalgia episode and a listener email on gender and job choice and the expectations that shape professional choices.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give contact info and the website.
